strengths: Significance: The reported improvements in molecular geometry are substantial. Table 1 shows 93.4% PoseBusters validity versus 84.6% for MolCRAFT, and median strain energy of 25.96 versus 195. These are useful advances for generating physically plausible ligand poses.

Evaluation: The paper evaluates 100 CrossDock targets and 120 MolGenBench targets, covering geometry, docking, chemical filters, and scaffold recovery. MolGenBench scaffold filter passing rates improve to 31.79% and 29.61% for seen and unseen targets, respectively.

Originality: Evolving endpoint distributions offer a plausible schedule-design approach for avoiding premature concentration in exponential interpolation. Combining Gaussian coordinates and Dirichlet chemical types within progressive parameter refinement is a potentially useful contribution.

Presentation and reproducibility: The manuscript provides training and sampling pseudocode, basic architecture and optimizer settings, detailed geometry results, and ablations of schedules and explicit bond generation.

Limitations and ethics: Appendix H.1.2 candidly distinguishes geometric plausibility from biological activity and acknowledges poor exact-molecule rediscovery on unseen targets. The impact statement recognizes potential misuse; no specific unresolved ethical violation is evident.
weaknesses: Soundness: Equation 9 is not a valid general solution of the continuity equation. For the minimal exponential family N(mu(t), 1), with T(x)=x and eta=mu, it gives u(x)=(x-mu) mu_dot, whereas the translating Gaussian requires u(x)=mu_dot. Substitution into the continuity equation disproves the proposed formula. Appendix F.2 introduces an unspecified scaling matrix rather than deriving Equation 9, and its claim that velocity must vanish at the mode is false for translation.

Soundness: The Fisher flow-matching equivalence in Appendix F.3 does not establish equivalence for the implemented objective. Equations 23–25 compare infinitesimal updates from a shared parameter state and divide KL by delta-t squared. Algorithm 1 and Appendix G instead compare true and predicted distributions at the same time, reconstructed from different endpoint predictions. Algorithm 2 repeatedly resamples from these reconstructed distributions. The paper does not connect these operations to the asserted velocity-matching objective or establish their marginal transport correctness.

Soundness: Equation 33 labels the Dirichlet objective as KL(p||p_hat), but its formula is KL(p_hat||p). Unlike the equal-covariance Gaussian case, this reversal changes optimization. The manuscript needs a consistent derivation and an unambiguous account of which objective was implemented.

Geometric interpretation: The product exponential family in Appendix F.1 has a block-diagonal Fisher metric; this construction alone does not introduce coupling between coordinates and chemical identities. Coupling can arise through the shared neural predictor, but the claimed geometric resolution of modality mismatch is not demonstrated. Moreover, Equation 7 generally defines a curved natural-parameter path when its endpoint moves, and Appendix D conflates exponential-connection straightness with Fisher–Rao curvature: a constant-variance Gaussian path does not make the ambient hyperbolic geometry flat.

Evaluation and originality: The comparisons omit particularly relevant cited methods, including MolPilot, FLOWR, MolPIF, and SLDM. Since the implementation uses a MolPilot-derived backbone with added gated attention and bond prediction, matched-backbone schedule comparisons are needed to isolate the proposed contribution. Failure of a sharply concentrated static endpoint is insufficient to establish superiority over well-tuned alternative schedules. No repeated-run uncertainty or paired target-level confidence intervals are reported.

Presentation and significance: Several superiority claims contradict the tables. Section 4.2 calls Vina Dock performance best, although TargetDiff achieves a better mean and median (-7.80/-7.91 versus -7.72/-7.88). The claim of outperforming all scaffold metrics is also incorrect: DecompDiff has higher scaffold Hit Rates in every Table 2 split. Scaffold matching and docking support computational promise, but do not establish biological activity or improved binding specificity.

Reproducibility: Important operational details remain unspecified, including the ligand-size sampling rule, coordinate preprocessing, complete gated-attention equations, endpoint discretization and numerical handling of Dirichlet parameters, evaluation software settings, and treatment of failed samples or postprocessing. Table 5 reports 98.60% connectivity while Table 1 reports 97.1%, requiring clarification of denominators or pipelines. These gaps, together with the mathematical inconsistencies, prevent reliable reconstruction and outweigh the promising empirical geometry results.

strengths: Significance: The reported improvements in molecular geometry are substantial. Table 1 reports 93.4% PoseBusters validity versus 84.6% for MolCRAFT, and median strain energy of 25.96 versus 195. Bond-length, angle, and torsion distributions provide additional evidence of improved geometric fidelity.

Evaluation: The study extends beyond docking scores to medicinal-chemistry filters and scaffold recovery on 120 MolGenBench targets. Scaffold filter pass rates and hit fractions improve over the evaluated baselines, including on targets absent from CrossDock.

Originality: Evolving endpoint distributions offer a potentially useful schedule-design perspective for joint continuous and discrete molecular generation. The ablations investigate endpoint evolution, categorical parameterization, smoothing, and explicit bond generation.

Presentation and transparency: The overall organization, algorithm descriptions, and detailed evaluation appendix are helpful. Appendix H.1.2 explicitly acknowledges very low exact-molecule rediscovery and failure on unseen targets. The impact statement acknowledges potential misuse; no concrete material ethical violation is apparent.
weaknesses: Soundness—incorrect sample-space velocity: Equation 9 does not generally satisfy the continuity equation. For the fixed-variance Gaussian family N(mu(t), 1), with sufficient statistic T(x)=x and natural parameter mu, it gives u(x)=(x-mu) times mu_dot. The correct translation velocity is mu_dot; substituting the proposed velocity into the continuity equation leaves a nonzero residual. Appendix F.2 asserts an unspecified scaling matrix rather than deriving the claimed formula. This undermines a central theoretical connection.

Soundness—objective equivalence is not established: Appendix F.3 correctly expands KL between infinitesimal updates from a shared parameter state into a Fisher-metric velocity loss. However, Appendix G derives the implemented coordinate loss from KL between two different intermediate distributions at the same time. These are different constructions, and their equivalence is not shown. Furthermore, Equation 33 labels the Dirichlet expression as KL(true || predicted), although the displayed expression is KL(predicted || true). These discrepancies affect the claimed Fisher flow-matching interpretation.

Originality and mechanism: The exponential-family product construction in Appendix F.1 has a block-diagonal Fisher metric and does not itself introduce dependencies between coordinates, atom types, and bonds. Dependencies can arise through the shared network and data mixture, but that does not establish the claimed geometric coupling or modality synchronization. Matched comparisons against BFN/PIF or alternative schedules using the same architecture are needed to distinguish the proposed contribution from schedule tuning.

Geometric interpretation: The manuscript sometimes conflates e-connection geodesics with Fisher–Rao metric geodesics. Although Section 3.1 distinguishes the connections, Appendix D.2 incorrectly claims that manifold curvature vanishes along a constant-variance Gaussian path. A horizontal horocycle is not an ambient Fisher–Rao geodesic, and the Gaussian manifold retains its curvature. The dynamic path in Equation 7 also need not itself be an e-geodesic.

Evaluation and attribution: Comparisons omit closely relevant methods discussed in the manuscript, particularly MolPilot and FLOWR. The architecture additionally introduces gated attention and explicit bond prediction, while the main endpoint ablation compares against a poorly performing static configuration. This establishes sensitivity to the chosen schedule but does not isolate the benefit over competitive, matched alternatives. No repeated-run variability or target-level confidence intervals are reported.

Presentation and claim accuracy: Several superiority statements contradict the tables. Section 4.2 claims the best Vina Dock performance, but TargetDiff is better in both mean (-7.80 versus -7.72) and median (-7.91 versus -7.88). The claim of outperforming across all scaffold metrics is also incorrect: DecompDiff has higher scaffold hit rates in every reported split. These should be corrected, and scaffold overlap should not be presented as confirmation that newly generated molecules are bioactive.

Reproducibility: Appendix A gives useful basic hyperparameters but leaves consequential details unresolved, including training duration in optimization steps, hardware, the ligand-size sampling policy, and final categorical decoding. Algorithm 2 reaches Dirichlet parameters equal to the network prediction at t=1: a soft prediction is not a deterministic categorical endpoint, while a hard one-hot vector contains invalid zero concentrations for an ordinary Dirichlet sampler. The required limiting or decoding procedure is unspecified, and the manuscript provides no code availability statement.

Overall assessment: The geometric-quality results could support a useful empirical contribution, and the honest limitations discussion is welcome. Nevertheless, incorrect central mathematical statements, an unproven connection between the theory and implemented objective, and insufficiently controlled comparisons prevent acceptance in the current form.

strengths: Significance: The reported improvements in molecular geometry are substantial. On CrossDock, Table 1 reports 93.4% PoseBusters validity versus 84.6% for MolCRAFT, and median strain energy of 25.96 versus 195. These are useful gains for generating physically plausible candidate structures.

Evaluation: The paper goes beyond docking scores by evaluating geometry, connectivity, medicinal chemistry filters, and scaffold recovery across two benchmarks. MolGenBench scaffold filter pass rates improve to 31.79% and 29.61% for the two target groups, and Table 4 provides useful ablations of endpoint evolution, categorical schedules, and bond generation.

Originality: Evolving the endpoint of an exponential-family interpolation is a plausible scheduling idea. Its application to joint coordinate, atom-type, and bond generation offers a potentially useful extension of existing parameter-refinement frameworks.

Presentation, reproducibility, and limitations: The paper includes training and sampling pseudocode, architecture and optimizer settings, and extensive supplementary results. It candidly acknowledges low absolute active-molecule recovery and failure to recover known active molecules for unseen targets. The impact statement recognizes potential harmful applications; no concrete ethical violation is apparent.
weaknesses: Soundness—incorrect sample-space velocity: Equation 9 and Appendix F.2 do not establish the claimed continuity-equation solution. A simple counterexample is the unit-variance Gaussian location family, with T(x)=x and η=μ. Equation 9 gives u(x)=(x−μ)μ̇, whereas translating this Gaussian requires u(x)=μ̇; substituting the proposed field into the continuity equation fails. Appendix F.2 introduces an unspecified scaling matrix rather than deriving the stated formula. This is a substantive error in the theoretical foundation.

Soundness—flow-matching equivalence is not demonstrated for the implemented objective: Appendix F.3 correctly states a local KL expansion for two infinitesimal updates from the same parameter state. However, Appendix G and Algorithm 1 instead compare intermediate distributions reconstructed from true and predicted endpoints. They do not derive the infinitesimal update objective used in the proof, including the dynamic endpoint derivative in Equation 8. Furthermore, Equation 33 labels the Dirichlet loss as KL(true || predicted), while its formula is KL(predicted || true). These discrepancies require reconciliation before the claimed Fisher flow-matching equivalence can be accepted.

Soundness and originality—geometric claims exceed what is established: The product-family construction in Appendix F.1 has a block-diagonal Fisher metric and does not itself introduce dependencies between coordinates and chemical types. Such dependencies can arise through the shared neural predictor, but the manuscript does not isolate a new geometric coupling mechanism. Appendix D also conflates exponential-connection geodesics with Fisher–Rao Riemannian geometry: restricting Gaussian variance to a constant does not make the ambient manifold's curvature vanish. The contribution needs a more precise distinction between a useful noise schedule and a demonstrated geometric advantage.

Evaluation and attribution: Comparisons omit particularly relevant methods discussed in the paper, including MolPilot, which addresses modality scheduling and supplies the cited backbone, and FLOWR. The model also changes gated attention and explicit bond generation. The existing ablations provide partial evidence, but a matched-backbone comparison against established scheduling or parameter-refinement methods is needed to attribute gains to EvoEGF. No uncertainty estimates or repeated-run results are reported, and the claimed efficiency is not supported by comparative sampling times or step-quality curves.

Presentation and significance—several superiority claims contradict the tables: Section 4.2 claims the best Vina Dock performance, but TargetDiff performs better in Table 1 on both mean and median. The claim of outperforming baselines across all scaffold metrics is also incorrect: DecompDiff has higher scaffold hit rates in every reported group in Table 2. Target specificity remains limited: most TAScores are below 10, none exceed 100, and exact active-molecule recovery is zero on unseen targets. The honest limitations discussion is welcome, but the abstract and conclusions should consistently distinguish geometric plausibility and scaffold overlap from demonstrated bioactivity.

Reproducibility: Appendix A provides a useful outline but leaves important implementation choices unresolved, including the actual ligand-size sampling rule, coordinate normalization, categorical output decoding, endpoint handling for Dirichlet parameters approaching zero, and evaluation filtering or postprocessing. The sampling algorithm ends with an insufficiently specified conversion from simplex distributions to discrete molecular labels. There is also an unexplained connectivity discrepancy between Table 1 (97.1%) and Table 5 (98.60%). These details matter for reproducing the unusually strong validity and strain-energy results.

strengths: Significance: The reported geometric improvements are substantial. On CrossDock, PB-Valid increases from MolCRAFT’s 84.6% to 93.4%, median strain energy decreases from 195 to 25.96, and connectivity reaches 98.6% (Table 1). Bond-length and bond-angle distributions provide additional evidence of improved structural plausibility.

Originality: Combining Gaussian and Dirichlet natural-parameter paths with evolving endpoints is a plausible methodological contribution. Appendix D usefully examines why moving endpoints can describe paths beyond scalar reparameterizations of fixed-endpoint interpolation.

Evaluation: The experiments cover geometric validity, docking proxies, scaffold rediscovery, and intermediate structures. Table 4 examines endpoint smoothing, categorical parameterization, explicit bond generation, and sampling steps; retaining 92.0% PB-Valid at 50 steps is practically encouraging.

Presentation and reproducibility: The overall motivation is understandable, and the appendices provide training and sampling pseudocode, architecture settings, optimizer details, hardware, and throughput.

Limitations and ethics: The manuscript candidly acknowledges low absolute rediscovery rates and zero full-molecule recovery on unseen MolGenBench targets. This appropriately limits the biological interpretation of improved geometry. The impact statement recognizes potential misuse; no concrete ethical violation is evident.
weaknesses: Soundness—training and flow interpretation are not adequately connected. Appendix H.3 derives a local flow-matching interpretation for updates from a common current parameter with errors proportional to the step size. Algorithm 1 instead compares ground-truth and predicted distributions reconstructed at the same time from their endpoints, without a step-size factor. Algorithm 2 reconstructs distributions from the original prior and resamples at every iteration. The manuscript does not establish that these operations satisfy the local-update assumptions or recover the intended marginal distribution. A valid conditional density path alone does not establish correctness of the learned sampler.

Soundness—the categorical loss has an inconsistent KL direction. Equation 13 and Algorithm 1 implement KL(Dir(alpha_hat) || Dir(alpha)), whereas Equation 48 explicitly identifies that expression as KL(Dir(alpha) || Dir(alpha_hat)), and Equation 11 uses the latter direction. Reverse KL is a legitimate objective, but its optimization behavior differs; the actual objective and its derivation must be reconciled.

Soundness—the central synchronization claim is stronger than the analysis supports. A product exponential family has a block-diagonal Fisher matrix, but this does not establish matched uncertainty reduction across coordinates, atom types, and bonds. Summing component KL divergences also does not eliminate dependence on category counts, numbers of bonds, or loss reductions. The intermediate-state results show earlier chemical validity, but do not isolate Fisher-based synchronization from schedule choice and architecture.

The geometric explanation contains substantive inaccuracies. An exponential-connection geodesic is generally not a Fisher–Rao Levi-Civita geodesic, and the evolving-endpoint trajectory need not itself be an e-geodesic. Appendix E.2’s assertion that fixing Gaussian variance makes manifold curvature vanish conflates a straight coordinate path with ambient Riemannian geometry. Equation 17 also gives the reciprocal of the stated natural-parameter slope, although its qualitative non-collinearity conclusion survives.

Originality and comparative significance remain insufficiently established. MolPilot, MolPIF/PIF, and SLDM are particularly relevant predecessors, yet there are no quantitative comparisons with them. Appendix F explicitly acknowledges that MolPilot has higher PB-Valid, while the main tables omit it. Comparisons against older released samples and a poorly performing fixed-endpoint variant do not adequately separate the proposed geometry from improved scheduling, gated attention, or bond modeling.

Several empirical claims overstate the tables. EvoEGF-Mol does not outperform every scaffold metric: DecompDiff has higher scaffold hit rates in all three Table 2 categories, and unseen-target hit recovery ties MolCRAFT. Its mean Vina Score and Vina Min are worse than MolCRAFT’s. For unseen targets, 24 of 35 TAScores are at most one. These results support improved geometric plausibility more convincingly than superior target-specific discovery or binding quality.

Reproducibility and statistical support are incomplete. The abstract’s code-availability statement provides no usable address. The manuscript leaves ligand-size sampling, coordinate normalization, final simplex-to-category decoding, categorical boundary stabilization, and loss aggregation insufficiently specified. These choices materially affect replication. No repeated-run uncertainty or target-level confidence intervals are reported, making smaller ablation differences difficult to interpret.

strengths: Significance: The reported geometric improvements are substantial. On CrossDock, PB-Valid increases from MolCRAFT’s 84.6% to 93.4%, median strain energy decreases from 195 to 25.96, and connectivity reaches 98.6% (Table 1). The detailed geometry distributions and PoseBusters checks provide complementary evidence.

Originality: Evolving Gaussian and Dirichlet endpoints within a shared natural-parameter formulation is a useful probability-path design. Appendix D provides a meaningful argument that the proposed Gaussian path generally cannot be reduced to scalar time reparameterization of a fixed-endpoint e-geodesic.

Evaluation: The paper goes beyond docking scores by evaluating chemical filters, scaffold recovery, intermediate states, and sampling-step sensitivity. The bond-free variant retains 90.8% PB-Valid, suggesting that explicit bond generation alone does not explain the gains.

Presentation and limitations: The manuscript is broadly organized and supplies algorithms, implementation settings, and extensive supplementary results. It candidly acknowledges the very low absolute active-molecule recovery and failure to recover exact known actives on unseen targets. The impact statement recognizes potential misuse; no specific material ethical violation is evident.
weaknesses: Soundness—training objective versus theoretical interpretation: Appendix H.3 derives a local Fisher-Rao velocity loss assuming true and predicted updates depart from the same parameter state and differ by O(Δt). However, Algorithm 1 and Appendix I compare distributions reconstructed independently from true and predicted endpoints at the same time t, without a Δt update. Their discrepancy need not vanish as Δt approaches zero. Thus, the stated infinitesimal flow-matching justification is not established for the implemented objective or the resampling procedure in Algorithm 2.

Soundness—incorrect KL direction: Equation 13 and Equation 48 implement KL(Dir(α̂t) || Dir(αt)), whereas Equation 48 identifies this as KL(pv,t || p̂v,t), and Equation 11 uses the latter direction. These objectives have different finite-error gradients and optima. Although both share a local Fisher expansion, that does not resolve the discrepancy in the actual training objective.

Soundness—synchronization is asserted more strongly than demonstrated: A product exponential family and block-diagonal Fisher metric do not establish aligned information gain or balanced supervision across modalities. The schedules still depend on chosen parameterizations, category counts, and a tuned λ. Tables 6–7 show earlier molecular validity, but do not directly measure coordinate/type uncertainty alignment or isolate Fisher calibration from schedule and architecture changes.

Evaluation and originality—critical comparisons are missing: Appendix F explicitly acknowledges that MolPilot achieves higher PB-Valid, yet omits its numerical results from the main comparisons despite its direct relevance to modality scheduling. Comparisons with PIF/MolPIF and relevant contemporary flow methods would also help establish the incremental contribution. The strongest fixed-endpoint ablation uses σ1 = 0.05 and near-one-hot types; failure of this configuration does not establish superiority over well-tuned regularized paths. Matched architecture and objective comparisons are needed to attribute gains to the proposed geometry.

Significance and presentation—several superiority claims exceed the results: Table 2 contradicts the statement that the method outperforms baselines across all scaffold metrics: DecompDiff has higher scaffold hit rates in every reported category, and unseen-target recovery ties MolCRAFT at 33. Table 1 also shows weaker average Vina Score and Vina Min than MolCRAFT. Scaffold recovery and pose validity support structural plausibility, but do not establish the biological activity or binding specificity suggested by parts of the discussion.

Reproducibility and statistical support: The abstract’s code-availability statement contains no link. Although useful hyperparameters are provided, atom-count selection, coordinate preprocessing, final simplex-to-category decoding, and numerical handling of boundary Dirichlet parameters remain insufficiently specified. Algorithm 2 ends with Dirichlet parameters equal to predicted type vectors: soft predictions need not yield deterministic categories, while exact one-hot predictions contain invalid zero concentrations. No repeated-run uncertainty or target-level confidence intervals are reported.

Mathematical presentation needs correction: Appendix E conflates straightness under the exponential connection with Fisher-Rao geometry. A constant-variance Gaussian path is a horocycle, not a Fisher-Rao geodesic, and restricting to it does not make the ambient manifold’s curvature vanish. These errors matter because geometric justification is central to the contribution. Together with the objective inconsistencies and incomplete comparisons, they prevent acceptance despite the promising empirical geometry results.

strengths: Significance: The reported geometric improvements are substantial. On CrossDock, EvoEGF-Mol achieves 93.4% PoseBusters validity versus 84.6% for MolCRAFT, reduces median strain energy from 195 to 25.96, and achieves 98.6% connectivity (Table 1). These are useful advances in generating physically plausible molecular structures.

Originality: Combining Gaussian and Dirichlet parameter paths with evolving endpoints provides an interesting extension of progressive parameter refinement to joint coordinate, atom, and bond generation. The dynamic-endpoint construction offers a potentially useful design perspective beyond fixed-endpoint interpolation.

Evaluation: The paper evaluates both geometric quality and scaffold rediscovery, including unseen targets and removal of training scaffolds. Table 4 provides informative ablations of endpoint evolution, Dirichlet parameterization, explicit bonds, smoothing, and sampling steps; 50-step sampling retains 92.0% validity.

Presentation and reproducibility: The main exposition is organized, and the appendices provide algorithms, architecture and optimizer settings, computational costs, detailed metric definitions, and per-check PoseBusters results.

Limitations and ethics: The manuscript candidly acknowledges low absolute rediscovery rates and the gap between geometric plausibility and biochemical activity. The impact statement recognizes potential misuse; no concrete ethical violation is evident.
weaknesses: Soundness—central theoretical justification: Appendix H.3 derives a Fisher-Rao velocity-matching interpretation for two infinitesimal updates from the same current parameter. However, Algorithm 1 and Appendix I compare full endpoint-induced distributions at the same time t, without a step-size factor or a requirement that their parameter discrepancy vanish with the step size. Algorithm 2 reconstructs parameters from the prior and a newly predicted endpoint and resamples. The manuscript does not establish that this procedure satisfies the assumptions of the local velocity argument or reproduces the intended marginal path. This is a substantive gap between the implemented method and its claimed transport interpretation.

Soundness—loss inconsistency: Equation 13 and Algorithm 1 implement KL(Dir(hat-alpha) || Dir(alpha)), whereas Equation 48 explicitly labels that expression as KL(Dir(alpha) || Dir(hat-alpha)). Unlike the equal-covariance Gaussian loss, these directions are not interchangeable. The intended objective and its derivation must be reconciled.

Soundness—synchronization and geometry: A block-diagonal Fisher metric and a shared time variable do not by themselves establish synchronized information acquisition across modalities. The Gaussian and Dirichlet schedules still determine their relative uncertainty trajectories, and Tables 6–7 measure intermediate validity rather than modality alignment directly. Appendix E.2 also conflates exponential-connection geometry with Fisher-Rao Riemannian geometry: restricting a Gaussian path to constant variance does not make the ambient manifold curvature vanish. These issues weaken the central geometric explanation.

Evaluation and originality: The most directly relevant comparison is missing from the quantitative tables. Appendix F identifies MolPilot as a state-of-the-art scheduling method and acknowledges that it has higher PoseBusters validity, but provides no complete comparison. Modern flow baselines discussed in Related Work are also absent. Since the implementation adds gated attention and explicit bond updates, a matched-backbone comparison is needed to isolate the proposed path from architectural changes. Failure of a sharply concentrated static endpoint alone does not establish superiority over well-tuned alternative schedules.

Presentation and significance: Several superiority claims exceed the results. Table 2 does not show improvements across all scaffold metrics: DecompDiff has higher hit rates, and MolCRAFT ties unseen-target hit recovery. MolCRAFT also has better average Vina Score and Vina Min in Table 1. Scaffold matching is evidence of rediscovery, not experimental confirmation of activity for the generated molecules. The contribution is strongest in geometric quality; the broader binding and discovery claims need narrowing.

Reproducibility and statistical support: The abstract's code-availability statement has no link. The exact ligand-size sampling policy, final conversion of Dirichlet samples into discrete labels, and handling of zero or near-zero concentration parameters are insufficiently specified. No repeated-run variability or target-level confidence intervals are reported. Given the substantial empirical promise, resolving these implementation details, theoretical inconsistencies, and comparison gaps could materially strengthen the work, but the current evidence does not justify acceptance.
